research_question: Is the manuscript's core novelty claim still defensible as of 2026-10: a documented failure / boundary condition for the inference 'bulk Floquet invariant constrains a protected non-Gaussian (Wigner-negativity) resource' in an open chiral Floquet SSH chain with Kerr nonlinearity? What prior or concurrent work (2019-2026) reports the absence, loss, or non-tracking of non-Gaussian resources / Wigner negativity under topology, and what work claims protection that could contradict us?
study_type: numerical open-quantum-systems study (stochastic master equation trajectories, matched paired design, out-of-sample frozen prediction, resource-theoretic witness certification)
population: two-step chiral Floquet SSH chains of 4 to 10 modes with local Kerr nonlinearity and edge-selective Lindblad loss
comparator: topological vs trivial sectors under identical dissipation, disorder (multiplicative loss noise), and initial cat state
outcomes: local Wigner-negativity contrast between sectors (sign change with size); grid-free displaced-Fock witness certification; dependence on dimerization, symmetry of the dissipator, and sub-period micromotion phase
field: open quantum systems, Floquet topological photonics/mechanics, non-Gaussian resource theory, Wigner negativity
